evidence.title: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index
evidence.summary: The snapshotted target change was -0.471 index points; it resolved to 'below recent range'.

evidence.title: What Are Financial Market Stress Indexes Showing?
evidence.domain: st. louis fed on the economy
evidence.summary: This article directly discusses the St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index (STLFSI), its recent revisions, and its relationship with other financial stress indexes. It highlights a divergence between the LIBOR and SOFR versions of the STLFSI, which is crucial for understanding the index's behavior around the target period.

evidence.title: The KCFSI suggests financial stress edged up in January but remained below its historical average.
evidence.domain: federal reserve bank of kansas city
evidence.summary: While focusing on the KCFSI, this source provides a detailed explanation of how financial stress indexes are constructed (principal component analysis) and interpreted (mean of zero, standard deviation of one). This methodological context is applicable to the STLFSI, which also uses principal component analysis.

evidence.title: Preliminary results from the January 2023 survey January 13, 2023
evidence.domain: university of michigan surveys of consumers
evidence.summary: This report provides insights into consumer sentiment, inflation expectations, and perceptions of borrowing costs in January 2023. These factors can influence financial market conditions and, consequently, financial stress indexes.

evidence.title: Financial stress index stays in 'danger' stage amid global tightening, credit crunch woes - The Korea Times
evidence.summary: This article discusses a financial stress index (FSI) in Korea, but its mention of 'global tightening' and 'credit crunch woes' indicates broader global financial conditions that could influence the US STLFSI.

evidence.title: US debt ceiling saga softens Fed's QT: McGeever
evidence.summary: This article discusses the impact of the US debt ceiling on the Federal Reserve's quantitative tightening (QT) policies. Changes in Fed policy and market liquidity can directly affect financial stress.

evidence.title: Financial Stress Index as a Generalized Indicator of Financial Instability
evidence.summary: This academic paper provides a general understanding of financial stress indexes as indicators of financial instability, offering a theoretical backdrop for interpreting the STLFSI's movements.
